answer: Reputation-Weighted Queue Position. Each identity's outbound work queues behind a score earned from completed tasks; a fresh identity starts at the back. To push a clone forward, the attacker must fund genuine work until its score rises, paying full compute and time per identity. A quill of proven history can't be transferred cheaply. The ocean of pending tasks absorbs fake accounts at the tail. Each message also carries a cipher tied to its queue slot, so duplicates collapse. Cost: one real task-completion cycle per clone, recurring.
